title: Sharp One-Third Stability of Brenier Maps
main_claim: Let rho be the uniform measure on a compact convex body K in R^d, d>=2, and let Y be compact. Then ||T_mu - T_nu||_{L^2(rho)} <= C(K,Y) W_2(mu,nu)^{1/3} for all mu, nu in Prob(Y), with an explicit constant C_*. The exponent 1/3 is sharp, even for K=Y=[-1,1]^d with three-atom targets, which disproves Letrouit's conjectured uniform square-root estimate.
coverage:
Read all six sections in full and checked every step of the main proof chain.
(1) Sharpness example: rechecked the cell masses, the symmetric-difference mass b/2, the pointwise identity |T-T~|^2 = 1_{AΔB} + b^2 1_B, W_2^2 = ab^2 (lower bound from the second coordinate), and the ratio exponent (1-3α)/2. Also checked the 5a^3/64 potential computation in the remark.
(2) Laguerre-cell calculus: face-integral derivatives, the null exceptional sets, connectivity of the face graph, and existence/uniqueness/C^1 of intercepts with prescribed masses (coercivity on H_m, the Lagrange-multiplier argument, and the implicit function theorem from G: H_m -> H_0 being an isomorphism).
(3) Midpoint coupling via the Knothe map: the diagonal-derivative product is |U|, the AM-GM step holds, and the change of variables for triangular maps is valid.
(4) Moment lemma: redid the algebra. The identity sum gamma_i(...) <= ∫Φ dρ holds; (α+β)/2 - γ <= δ^2/(8γ); the Cauchy-Schwarz step gives A <= 5R^2 B; the bounds α^2/M <= 8γ and B <= 2E hold; 2 + 16·5·2 = 162. The derivative limit is correct.
(5) Finite stability: the cyclical-monotonicity argument keeps interior sites distinct. The duality identity sum r_i DM_i[q,0] = -sum v_i·DB_i[q,0] follows from symmetry of g_ij and b_ij together with the differentiated mass constraint. Solvability of DM[q,0] = m r uses sum m_i r_i = 0. The Cauchy-Schwarz bound gives sqrt(E_r) <= sqrt(C0) R w. Endpoint limits and the identification of the limit slopes with mu and nu are justified.
(6) Gradient interpolation: the convexity bounds 0 <= δ_u <= 2L, the per-slice telescoping bound of 2Lh, an excluded set of length at most h per slice, and the constants 12d and 24+4=28. With h = w^{2/3} this gives C_*.
(7) Extension to arbitrary targets: the Cauchy argument via nets, the limit pushforward, optimality and uniqueness from the limiting Fenchel identity, and the bound W_2(mu_n,nu_n) <= W_2 + 2ε_n.
No gaps found. Python was not needed beyond hand-checking constants.
